workarounds.symptom: llm 0.38: Templates, fragment files passed to `-f` and Python files passed to `--functions` are now read as UTF-8, falling back to the system default encoding for files that are not valid UT
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Templates, fragment files passed to `-f` and Python files passed to `--functions` are now read as UTF-8, falling back to the system default encoding for files that are not valid UTF-8. Previously, on systems with a different default encoding such as Windows, a file containing non-ASCII characters could cause a `UnicodeDecodeError`. Thanks, [CJstate](https://github.com/CJstate). [#1893](https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1893). Upstream PR #1893. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1893)

workarounds.workaround: Fix: OpenAI Chat Completions models no longer crash with a `JSONDecodeError` when the model returns tool call arguments that are not valid JSON, such as arguments cut off part way through. The tool is not run, and the error is sent back to the model as the tool result so it can try again. Thanks, [Usama Iftikhar](https://github.com/pseudo-usama). [#1887](https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1887). Upstream PR #1887. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1887)

This also stopped `llm templates list` from working while such a template was present. Thanks, [Steven Huang](https://github.com/remote-controlled-man). workarounds.symptom: `llm embed` with an unknown model says no default is set, or shows a traceback
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Report unknown embedding models instead of a missing default. Target files: llm/cli.py, tests/test_embed_cli.py. `llm embed` and `llm embed-multi` treated an `UnknownModelError` as if no model had been given, so `-m nope` printed "You need to specify an embedding model (no default model is set)". Creating a new collection with `llm embed newc id -m nope` didn't catch it and showed a traceback. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1882)

workarounds.symptom: Error in llm chat due to invalid key \e[d from case conversion in key bindings (Windows 11)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Skip invalid readline arrow-key bindings on Windows, fixes #585. Target files: llm/cli.py. The win32 branch in `chat()` passes GNU-readline syntax (`bind -x '\e[D: backward-char'`) to `readline.parse_and_bind()`. On Windows that is pyreadline3, which lowercases key descriptions and raises `IndexError: Not a valid key` for escape sequences like `\e[D` — exactly the traceback in this issue. Reporters in the thread confirmed chat starts normally once the bindings are removed, and pyreadline3 provides its own arrow-key handling, so t... (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1809)

workarounds.symptom: llm 0.37.2: `llm openai endpoint list --json` no longer crashes with a `TypeError` when `extra-openai-models.yaml` contains an unquoted date, such as `api_version: 2024-02-01`. Thanks, [Steven
workarounds.workaround: Fix: `llm openai endpoint list --json` no longer crashes with a `TypeError` when `extra-openai-models.yaml` contains an unquoted date, such as `api_version: 2024-02-01`. Thanks, [Steven Huang](https://github.com/remote-controlled-man). [#1850](https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1850). Upstream PR #1850. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1850)

workarounds.symptom: `llm openai endpoint add` writes unparseable YAML when the existing list is indented
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Preserve YAML layout when adding OpenAI endpoints. Target files: llm/default_plugins/openai_models.py, tests/test_openai_endpoint_add.py. Adding an endpoint to an indented block list wrote the new entry at column zero, leaving `extra-openai-models.yaml` unparseable. Appending after an explicit `...` document end marker caused the same failure, so subsequent model-loading commands stopped working. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1865)

workarounds.symptom: Enable mac clipboard via pngpaste (Support unseekable attachments)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Support pipe paths for CLI attachments. Target files: llm/cli.py, tests/test_attachments.py. Attachments passed through Bash process substitution, such as `llm "Describe this image" -a <(cat image.png)`, could not be detected because MIME probing expects a seekable file. With an explicit `--at` type, hashing and subsequent reads could instead consume the pipe and lose its content. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1857)

workarounds.symptom: `--no-stream` crashes with AttributeError when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint omits `usage`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix crash when a non-streaming Chat Completions response has no usage. Target files: llm/default_plugins/openai_models.py, tests/test_cli_openai_models.py. `Chat.execute()` and `AsyncChat.execute()` called `completion.usage.model_dump()` without checking that `usage` is set. OpenAI-compatible servers can omit the `usage` key or send `"usage": null`, and every `--no-stream` prompt against them failed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'model_dump'`. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1698)
